solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Blown, three sheets to the wind (6)

blocks.note: first definition: money blown is squandered
second definition: an old sailors' phrase for very drunk

annotation.walkthrough: 'Three sheets to the wind' comes from sailing: a ship with its sheets (ropes) loose lurches like a drunk. Wasted is modern slang for drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: squandered, as blown money is, and slang for very drunk.

entries.clue: Around America, a large body of water diverted (6)

indicators.note: 'Around' has one piece encircle another, as a road goes around a town

blocks.note: taken as written
MED is short for the Mediterranean Sea; it goes around US
US = United States

annotation.surface: A navigator steering around a big sea on the way to America.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'diverted' as rerouted, but it means entertained. MED is the usual crossword shorthand for the Mediterranean.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the entertainment sense: a diversion is an amusement.

entries.clue: Identify a report in story that may be panned by Italians? (11)

definitions.text: that may be panned by Italians?

indicators.note: 'in' places A TELL inside the story, as words sit inside a tale

blocks.note: to tag something is to label or identify it
a story is a fib, a lie; it goes around the next two pieces
taken as written
to tell is to report

annotation.surface: Asks us to spot a news item buried in a tale that Italian critics would slate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Panned' pretends to mean slated by critics; the pasta is cooked in a pan. The question mark flags this cryptic definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is Italian ribbon pasta, cooked in a pan by Italians.

entries.clue: Undertake something to chew on, stuff on a programme (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, RAM sits on top of A

blocks.note: to do a task is to undertake it
cud is what a cow chews
to stuff is to ram in
taken as written

annotation.surface: A to-do list: take something on, find something to chew over, and cram a TV schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something to chew on' suggests food for thought; cud is the cow's literal version.
annotation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a TV programme dramatising real events.

entries.clue: Change required around odd parts of Antrim — might this be tried? (8)

indicators.note: 'around' has PENCE surrounding the other letters, as a wall goes around a town
'odd' means the odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth

blocks.note: loose change is pennies, pence
A-n-T-r-I-m

annotation.surface: Someone wanting coins while touring County Antrim in Northern Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole question: your patience is what gets tried. Pence is the British small change.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: we say someone's patience is tried, so the clue asks what might be tried.

entries.clue: Exercise hard, a cheek aloft (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: concrete that is set is hard
taken as written
lip = cheek, impudence

annotation.surface: A gym instructor urging a hard workout, face held high.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like a body part to lift; it is impudence, LIP.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Pilates is one particular regime of exercise.

entries.clue: Body like that shouldering rock (5)

indicators.note: SO carries TOR on its shoulders: in a down clue TOR sits above

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
so = like that, in that way

annotation.surface: A figure like Atlas, bearing a boulder on its shoulders.
annotation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England; 'shouldering' puts it on top.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the trunk, the body without head or limbs.

entries.clue: Going topless, flesh to put away? (3)

indicators.note: drop the top letter, in a down clue the first

blocks.note: flesh is MEAT; 'going topless' removes its first letter

annotation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone stripping off and then covering up again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests covering the flesh; it is slang for eating a lot.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: to put away a meal is to consume it greedily.

entries.clue: Force in liquid, bottling a drink (4,4)

indicators.note: fluid letters flow into a new order
the rearranged letters hold A inside

blocks.note: the letters of FORCE IN, rearranged
taken as written, held after the C

annotation.surface: Pushing a drink into a liquid, like forcing a bottle into a cooler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like the physics term or F; here it is anagram fodder along with 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: Café noir is French for black coffee, a drink.

entries.clue: Operative relocating us, a girl needing Charlie to fill in (8)

indicators.note: 'relocating' means moving to a new place, so the letters of US A GIRL move into a new order
C goes into the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the letters of US A GIRL, rearranged
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A secret agent moving house and needing someone called Charlie to step in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Operative' looks like a spy, a noun; it is the adjective, to do with operations.
annotation.definitionFit: Surgical means relating to operations, operative.

entries.clue: OK swimmer keeping in trim, doing the backstroke? (6)

indicators.note: RAY holds the other piece
a backstroke goes backwards, so FIT reads in reverse

blocks.note: a ray is a fish, a swimmer
in trim = in good shape, fit

annotation.surface: A swimmer keeping in shape by doing backstroke lengths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a person in the surface; in crosswords it is often a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to OK a proposal is to give it formal approval.

entries.clue: Losing tie, I’m sorry to have got involved (6)

indicators.note: EH gets caught up inside BIND

blocks.note: to tie is to bind; it goes around EH
'Eh?' is what you say for 'I'm sorry, what?'

annotation.surface: An apology for getting mixed up in a lost match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm sorry' is not an apology but a request to repeat, EH. 'Losing tie' looks like a lost cup match; 'tie' is BIND.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting sense: a side trailing on the scoreboard is in arrears.

entries.clue: Figure you grind down (8)

blocks.note: thou is old-fashioned 'you'
to sand wood is to grind it down

annotation.surface: An instruction to someone to wear down a statue or shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a shape or statue; here it is a number.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a figure is a number, and this is one particular number.

entries.clue: Journeying afar, vaster place to tour around (5,6)

indicators.note: the letters wander about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of VASTER PLACE, rearranged

annotation.surface: A traveller looking for somewhere bigger to explore on a long trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vaster place' looks like a destination; it is the fodder, and 'to tour around' sets the letters wandering.
annotation.definitionFit: Space travel is journeying very far indeed.

entries.clue: Ancient orcas swimming across the Pacific, say? (12)

indicators.note: the letters swim about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of ANCIENT ORCAS, rearranged

annotation.surface: Old killer whales crossing the Pacific Ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an example, flagged by 'say': the Pacific is one ocean to cross.
annotation.definitionFit: Transoceanic means crossing an ocean, as across the Pacific.

entries.clue: In hostile environment, soldier that’s whipped in France? (9)

indicators.note: 'In' puts the soldier inside the hostile environment, as a trooper deep in enemy land

blocks.note: a chilly welcome is a hostile one; it goes around ANT
a soldier ant

annotation.surface: A soldier in enemy territory being flogged by the French.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' suggests a flogging; it is cream. 'Soldier' is an ant, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Chantilly is sweetened whipped cream, named after a French town.

entries.clue: Agent in male clothes (8)

indicators.note: as a verb, MISTER clothes IN, wrapping around it

blocks.note: Mister is the title for a man; it goes around IN
taken as written

annotation.surface: A spy dressed in men's clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to dress, so one piece wraps the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A minister is an agent acting on someone else's behalf.

entries.clue: Measure of his work written with determination, mere poet (7,5)

indicators.note: the measure is written next to the determination

blocks.note: strength of will
an iamb is a metrical foot, a measure of verse
a mere is a lake

annotation.surface: Weighing up the output of a poet who writes with grit but is merely a poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only'; it is the old word for a lake. 'His work' means poetry, which is measured in feet such as the iamb.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer is one specific poet: Blake wrote 'Jerusalem' and 'The Tyger'.

entries.clue: In sheets and blankets etc, not as much being darned (7)

indicators.note: 'In' puts one piece inside the bedding, as a sleeper lies in bed

blocks.note: bedding makes a bed; it goes around LESS
less = not as much

annotation.surface: Someone darning holes in the bed linen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Darned' pretends to mean mended; it is the mild oath, as in 'I'm blessed if I know'.
annotation.definitionFit: Blessed and darned are both mild euphemisms for damned.

entries.clue: Design one has to beat (6)

blocks.note: first definition: an inked picture on the skin
second definition: a rhythmic drumming or tapping, as on a parade ground

annotation.surface: An idea you have to defeat.
annotation.walkthrough: A tattoo is a design on the skin, and also a drumbeat or a rhythmic tapping.
annotation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a skin design and a drum signal.

entries.clue: One warmed by this retrospective poem, stay (8)

indicators.note: looking back, so the poem reads backwards

blocks.note: 'If' is Kipling's famous poem
to stay somewhere is to reside

annotation.surface: A poet looking back on their work while staying by a warm hearth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'If—' by Rudyard Kipling is a hugely popular British poem, which makes it a crossword favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by effect: the hearthside spot is where one sits to be warmed.

entries.clue: Perfect situation, part equally distributed served up (5)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow
in a down clue, up means reading backwards

blocks.note: equaLLY DIstributed

annotation.surface: An ideal set-up where shares are dished out fairly.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters straddle two words; in a down clue 'served up' means read from the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a blissful, ideal scene or state of affairs.

entries.clue: Sculptures possibly in bronze material (6)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the art inside the bronze colour, as a statue is cast in metal

blocks.note: bronze and tan are both brown shades; TAN goes around ART
sculptures are an example of art

annotation.surface: Statues cast in bronze.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bronze' looks like the metal of the sculptures; it is the colour, TAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Tartan is a checked woollen cloth, a material.

entries.clue: Podgy middle in sight (6)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the middle inside the sight, as something held in view

blocks.note: to sight something is to spy it; SPY goes around TUM
tum = tummy, your middle

annotation.surface: A paunch coming into view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sight' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to spot. TUM is British for tummy.
annotation.definitionFit: Podgy and stumpy both describe someone short and thick.

entries.clue: Crew from the galleon, all at the bottom (3)

indicators.note: take every word's bottom letter, its last in a down clue

blocks.note: froM thE galleoN

annotation.surface: A galleon's sailors all down below decks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All at the bottom' reads like sailors below deck; in a down clue it means every word's last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship's crew are its hands, so the plain word for them serves.

entries.clue: Drinking one huge quantity of wine, fair to drool (8)

indicators.note: SALE takes in I VAT, as if swallowing it

blocks.note: a sale, like a craft fair, is a place to sell; it goes around I VAT
I is the Roman numeral one
wine is made in vats

annotation.surface: A drinker downing a vat of wine at a fair, drooling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a sale. A vat holds wine by the thousand litres.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to produce saliva, typically at the thought of food.

entries.clue: Cordial communication ultimately distributed in plate? (4-4)

indicators.note: the letters are shared out into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of communicatioN

annotation.surface: A friendly letter finally sent out on a dinner plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plate' looks like crockery; it is armour plate, as on an ironclad warship.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ironclad is covered in iron plate.

entries.clue: Chicken like a canary (6)

blocks.note: first definition: cowardly
second definition: a canary's colour

annotation.walkthrough: Both definitions look like birds; one means cowardly and the other is a colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Chicken means cowardly, or yellow; canaries are yellow.
